findings.expected: Only what Vitalis decided is attributed to him. The OD-6 record (review/opus-5-5-d2-confirm/owner-decisions-2026-11-24-d2.md) fixes: one mark from A/B; all A/B F.T.; M/DM as usual; own figures = accuracy; changed object/difficulty or no solution = no MR; feedback names the misread. findings.actual: The OD-6 row is classed 'binding owner decision', and its departure reads 'Owner chose one earned A/B deduction per eligible datum in its first-use part ... Earliest eligible earned A/B in declared order; none earned means no deduction or borrowing. No later-part second deduction.' OWNER-CHECKPOINT:15 'OD-6 settled: one eligible first-use A/B deduction'. HANDOVER:17 'OD-6 is binding: ... one earliest eligible earned A/B deduction at first use per datum'. recipe-contract:303 'OD-6 binds ... with one eligible earned A/B deduction in the datum's first-use part'. Mitigation: the row state says 'application of the rule is part of the pending exact candidate confirmation', and the MR03 authority cell scopes the owner allocation correctly ('MR-1 from A/B, all A/B F.T., own-figure errors excluded').
findings.evidence: The Cambridge PDF3 Penalties text (rendered) says nothing on per-datum units, first-use part, slot choice or deferral, and it also allows MR-2 at coordination. The owner record says only 'costs one mark'. This is the same kind of error as D2-S04 (tariff attributed to OD-4), now in the central OD-6 register row. By the brief's literal wording ('non-owner interpretation presented as an owner decision') this is at the margin of design-blocking. I grade it should-fix because the content came from our own prompt, the row state flags application as pending, and approval of the manifest would cover it anyway.
findings.repair: Split the OD-6 row and the HANDOVER/contract sentences. Owner (OD-6): MR-1 from A/B, all A/B F.T., M/DM usual, own-figure/changed-object exclusions, feedback names the misread. Proposed operational unit (reviewer-prescribed in REPAIR-D3-PROMPT, planner-settled; approval pending): once per datum at first use, earliest eligible earned A/B, no borrowing or deferral, distinct data one mark each. Mirror this split in the MR03 rule cell.

findings.locator: subject-rules.md:67 ('If the first-use part earns no A/B, deduct nothing there or later'); calculus-design.json misread_policy.deduction.if_none ('do not transfer a charge to a later part' / motion 'do not deduct from M/DM or another part'); trig/visual policies ('do not defer'); WOs e.g. WB8227-motion-integration.md:56, WB8227-vector-geometry.md:94,108
findings.expected: OD-6: a genuine misread 'costs one mark, deducted from the A or B marks'. A rule under which an eligible misread costs nothing should be shown to Vitalis as a choice.
findings.actual: If the first-use part earns no A/B (e.g. because of an unrelated named error), no deduction is made anywhere. Later parts still earn A/B by OD-6 F.T. on the misread value. Vector: OB sign misread + named wrong resultant in (a) gives a:M1 only, then (b) 4/4 F.T. = 5/7, the same as a learner with the same named error and no misread. Motion: V 12->21 + wrong -V/k factor gives 0/2 + 3/3 = 3/5, the same as without the misread. CONVENTION:108 (no maximum) is still met, because every part has at least one A/B criterion (checked over all 27 parts).
findings.evidence: Mark types: vector (a) B1/M1/A1, (b) B1/M1/M2/A1 (WO:94); motion E1/E2 B1, E3 B1, E4 M1, E5 A1 (WO:47-48); exemplar vector :57 gives 5/7 for the canonical wrong-resultant learner. Our D3 prompt said 'If there are no A or B marks to deduct from, nothing is deducted'. In these cases later-part A/B marks do exist, so 'do not transfer' is the planner's narrower reading.
findings.repair: Put the choice to Vitalis inside the OD-6 approval: either keep part-local no-deferral (state that such misreads can be costless), or take the one mark from the first earned A/B in a later part that uses the same datum. Add the vector 5/7-vs-4/7 fixture either way.
